subject: Request: Multi-year rate sealing + renewal protection for MedTech
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-14T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: MedTech 3yr commitment — request for multi-year rate sealing + renewal protection

Hi team,

Quick escalation: MedTech (Anna Peters / Procurement) verbally committed to a 3-year consumption commitment if we can offer a firm rate for the first 24 months (price-sealed) and an uplift cap of no more than +8% on renewal years thereafter. They also want an explicit "renewal protection" clause that prevents unilateral list-price increases exceeding that cap if they renew within the commitment window.

Key commercial asks:
- 3yr term, $2.4M ARR year 1-2 baseline consumption (metered)
- Price sealed for 24 months, then renewal uplift capped at +8% YoY
- Automatic right to termination for material price leaps at renewal (they want this as protection)
- Minor SOW edits (attached)

Attachments: Deal_Deck_9.14.pptx, MedTech_SOW_v3.pdf, draft clause in exec_approval_template.docx

Why I need exec: this is outside standard 3-year guardrails — uplift cap is tighter than our typical 12% cap and the renewal protection language creates contractual risk if we cannot match capacity/region fallback. MedTech is a high-reference buyer in healthcare; losing them reduces our APAC expansion story.

Asks: 
1) Deal desk approval for the sealed 24-month price + 8% renewal cap (or guidance on a counter)
2) Legal/Finance sign-off path and any material guardrails we should add (e.g., limited to existing deployment regions, pre-agreed burst pricing)
3) Exec sign-off to proceed to DocuSign if approved

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick clarifying Qs for pricing/ops before we move to execs:
1) Is the sealed price tied to a model catalog / specific instance types (e.g., quantized 8-bit vs FP16)? Need to avoid open-ended costs if they request higher-cost variants later.
2) Can we require volume tiers (e.g., <X TB tokens/month triggers migration to dedicated pool with separate pricing) so their usage profile is bounded?
3) Are they requesting prior-rights to capacity in a region (this amplifies operational risk).

If answers are favorable, I can draft a conditional approval memo for Irene with proposed guardrails.

-L

Laura — answers inline:
1) We are proposing the sealed price tied to the "Redwood Standard" model variants listed in the deck (pages 4-6): quantized 8-bit recommended, with explicit exclusions for experimental/recent-release model family X. I will annotate the SOW to call this out.
2) Yes — proposed contract has tiered thresholds. If they exceed the top tier for two months in a row, pricing re-evaluation can be triggered (we proposed a cap on the re-evaluated uplift to ensure fairness).
3) They asked about regional preference for EU/US failover for latency; nothing that constitutes reserved dedicated capacity. We should include language that we will provide "best-effort" region continuity and cannot guarantee reserved capacity without Dedicated purchase.

I added the suggested guardrails into exec_approval_template.docx (attached) — draft conditional approval memo is in section 2.

Jordan

Team — quick finance POV:
- The sealed-price for 24 months with an 8% uplift cap materially compresses revenue upside versus our benchmark (12%). We need to preserve: (a) explicit clause that uplift cap applies only to base subscription unit price and not to separately metered overage/add-ons; (b) a mid-term true-up mechanism if average monthly usage >+35% of baseline for 3 consecutive months.
- Confirmed credit terms: Net 45 standard for this tier; procurement asked for Net 60 — counterproposal: Net 45 with an automated early-payment 1.5% credit.

If legal is okay with renewal protection language limited to the uplift cap and subject to our availability SLA, finance can live with it.

-dk

Team — reviewed the memo and attachments. Appreciate the conditional guardrails; I have three decisions and one conditional approval: 

1) Executive approval granted for a 24-month sealed price and an 8% renewal uplift cap, provided all of the following are contractually required: 
   - The sealed price applies only to the explicitly enumerated "Redwood Standard" model variants in the SOW; exclusions for experimental families are included.
   - Uplift cap applies only to base unit price; metered overages and add-ons may be charged separately and are explicitly excluded from the cap.
   - A mid-term true-up is triggered if average monthly usage exceeds 35% of the baseline for 3 consecutive months (finance will define the reconciliation flow).
   - Renewal protection clause limited to customers who remain within 110% of baseline usage in the prior 12 months and have not requested dedicated capacity.
2) Net terms: approve Net 45 with 1.5% early-pay credit instead of Net 60.
3) Legal: marriage-to-Legal to insert the conditional termination right tied to material price leaps but require that termination is subject to a 60-day cure period and a customer success remediation plan.

Conditional approval expires in 7 business days unless DocuSign envelope is executed. Please flag any unresolved material redlines immediately.

I will sign off on the exec approval template once Legal confirms the limited termination language and CS has the remediation playbook attached.

-Irene
